title: Retail trends 2026
subtitle: 5 forces reshaping the retail landscape

overview.summary: Five powerful trends are reshaping the future of retail, redefining how customers discover, decide, and buy. What’s inside: Moments over merchandise; The year of the private label; Searchless retail; Invisible AI; Trust as a profit driver.
overview.cover_note: 2026 Retail trends — 5 forces reshaping the retail landscape.

sections.heading: 1. Moments over merchandise
sections.summary: Post‑pandemic experience spending has become a lasting shift. Global travel is projected to grow 5.8% annually through 2032, while U.S. unit sales remain flat, indicating inflation rather than intention drives growth. Retailers must find new margin in an experience‑led market.
actions: Offer an experience (e.g., on‑site cooking classes; in‑store bars).
Capitalize on orbital purchases (e.g., complementary products for experience contexts).
Contextualize what is already personalized with real‑time offers.
insights: Travel and hospitality experiences lead luxury spending, outpacing fashion, cars, and beauty among high and ultra‑high net worth individuals.
To create meaningful brand moments, align brand identity with customer insight; favor participatory, community‑oriented experiences.

quotes.text: Retailers shouldn’t think of the experience economy as an opportunity. It’s a necessity.
quotes.attribution: Jessica Leitch, Head of frog - North America

sections.heading: 2. The year of the private label
sections.summary: Private labels are no longer just budget buys—70% of shoppers earning over $100,000 now choose their grocery store based on them; growth is strong but may be slowing, pushing retailers to innovate, expand assortments, and premiumize.
stats: 44% of shoppers are buying private‑label or low‑cost brands over name brands.
When switching to a cheaper alternative, top factors: 66% positive user reviews; 60% money‑back guarantees/return policies; 58% clear quality certifications.
7 in 10 consumers say small indulgences help them cope with financial stress (71%).
actions: Analyze shopper needs and trends using first‑party data.
Pilot and iterate based on feedback to upgrade quality.
Prioritize quality and differentiation around distinct value niches.

sections.heading: 3. The future of retail is searchless
sections.summary: Retail is moving from SEO to GEO (generative engine optimization). One in five of Walmart’s referral clicks in August came from ChatGPT, up 15% from July; 46% of shoppers make purchases based on AI recommendations and 46% are willing to order via AI tools.
actions: Shift from search to suggestion via AI/GenAI using behavioral, contextual, transactional signals.
Optimize for algorithmic visibility with stronger product/content tagging.
Engineer moments of serendipity with shoppable content, live commerce, and timely notifications.
callouts: Walmart announced a partnership with OpenAI to enable shopping through ChatGPT (Instant Checkout); early adoption may stall if recommendations fail to meet expectations.

quotes.text: Early adoption of AI-powered search is surging, but it may stall—or even retreat—if AI recommendations fail to meet expectations.
quotes.attribution: Dreen Yang, Global Lead, Consumer Products and Retail, Capgemini

sections.heading: 4. Invisible AI is expected
sections.summary: Consumers want seamless, frictionless, personalized experiences; 71% want Gen AI‑integrated shopping interactions (vs. 56% last year). Transparency builds confidence even when the tech stays in the background.
stats: 71% are concerned about lack of clarity in how AI collects/uses personal data.
52% will switch retailers for better data protection policies.
actions: Establish visible guardrails for privacy, security, and ethical use.
Keep humans in the loop with clear escalation and support.
sections.example: Visual AI can monitor self‑checkout to detect friction and recommend process improvements, operating silently to make experiences seamless.

quotes.text: Transparency builds confidence, even when the tech stays in the background.
quotes.attribution: Mark Ruston, Global Retail Lead, Capgemini

sections.heading: 5. Trust is the new profit driver
sections.summary: Margins are increasingly earned through trust as media, commerce, and operations converge. Build trust through the 3 Cs—consistency, care, contextualization—and add clarity to encourage data sharing.
stats: 36% trust products and suggestions shared by Gen AI tools.
66% trust a digital assistant more when it provides clear explanations.
actions: Care through actions that reflect customer values.
Clarity on how personal data is used to enrich experiences.
execution_notes: Participate in digital conversations: join Reddit threads, work with influencers, and create high‑quality content to build transparent experiences.
